newsitem.title: GERMANY: Fewer German construction orders in first 5 months.
newsitem.headline: Fewer German construction orders in first 5 months.

text.p: The German building industry remained in a slump during the first five months of 1997 with incoming orders down from a year ago, the German Building Industry Association said on Thursday.

Construction was especially weak in east Germany where incoming orders fell a real 12.6 percent, the association said in a statement. In west Germany, building was also weak with orders down four percent from a year ago.

Faltering demand also depressed construction employment with the number of workers in the industry falling 10.6 percent in west Germany to 819,000 and dropping 13.8 percent in east Germany to 372,000.

Although the association did not give a reason for the weak orders report, building in Germany has been severely depressed by weak economic growth which has curtailed investment spending and made consumers nervous about making major purchases.
In May alone, incoming orders in east Germany declined 16.9 percent and 4.2 percent in west Germany.

The only bright spot in the report for the first five months came from individual homes, with the number of approved building applications in east Germany increasing 19.2 percent to 18,400 in the first five months from a year ago.
In west Germany, the number of approved building applications for new homes increased 4.7 percent to 46,000.
But the association said the increase in demand for new homes would still not make up for weak demand in multi-storey apartment buildings.
Incoming orders for commercial building projects also fell, declining 15.5 percent in the east and 3.9 percent in the west.
